record.file_problem: none; full paper and appendices are present
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies how measured tangent-feature properties and a proposed complexity measure relate to generalization, using different measurements from the versions listed.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results on label corruption, feature alignment, effective rank, and a proposed complexity measure. Results cited from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: Figure 6 reports training and test error as width increases for a one-hidden-layer MNIST MLP and a CIFAR-10 VGG19, all trained to cross-entropy 0.01. These results bear on V2 despite the paper's focus on a new complexity measure. The supplied text does not reveal the curves' direction reliably enough for a verdict.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors interpret dynamical tangent-feature alignment as feature selection and compression that may act as implicit regularization. Their trajectory-based complexity measure is heuristic and correlates with generalization gaps in the reported sweeps; they do not establish a neural-network generalization bound or a causal explanation.
record.recipe_differences: Studies tangent-feature dynamics and a proposed complexity measure; it does not reproduce the original memorization/generalization experiments or the magnitude-aware sharpness measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Label corruption level, evaluation on training versus test examples, easy versus difficult examples, network depth, and learning rate are reported as affecting alignment or effective-rank dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: Effective rank drops early and rebounds during overfitting under high label noise; tangent features increasingly align with labels and align faster with easy examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tangent-feature geometry changes with task learning and overfitting, with preferential alignment to easier patterns.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed trajectory-based complexity measure reflects the generalization-gap shape across width and corruption sweeps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A complexity measure based on accumulated update norms and tangent-feature norms tracks generalization gaps in the tested settings.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 24th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS) 2021; PMLR Volume 130
record.problems: Most trajectories and comparisons are figure-only; the text gives qualitative descriptions without uncertainty estimates. The complexity-measure comparisons are reported qualitatively, and the authors describe the proposed measure as heuristic.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and fully random-label training, near-perfect random-label fitting, and chance held-out accuracy under fully random labels.
An explicitly identified interpolation threshold, training to convergence without explicit regularization, and the downsampled CIFAR-10 one-hidden-layer ReLU setting are not established.
Convolutional versus fully connected accuracy comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparisons and tuning-dependent differences.
Batch-size comparisons under matched epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm and margin measures. Output sensitivity to perturbations in Figure 7 does not supply these tests.
Removal of highly memorized examples, retraining, and comparison with random removal.

missing.what: Separate training and test errors at each tested width, identifying which widths interpolate. R5 and R7 mention these curves but record only the complexity-measure comparison; the supplied text does not permit reliable recovery of their direction or values.
missing.locator: Figure 6, MNIST hidden-size and CIFAR-10 channel-count panels; Section 4.2

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for the listed versions. No V2 label is assigned because the supplied figure text preserves axes and captions but not readable curve trajectories. Missing portions of the experiment are not evidence against V2.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report the specified comparison of near-perfect fitting of fully random labels with held-out accuracy at chance, alongside natural-label performance for the same recipes.
Although width is varied, the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU sweep past the zero-training-error interpolation threshold and its test-error behavior are not reported.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks or test local connectivity.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD.
Does not compare batch sizes or large-batch training.
Measures tangent-feature alignment, effective rank, and a proposed complexity measure, but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with the listed norm- and margin-based measures.
Does not remove memorized examples and retrain.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Measured effective rank of tangent kernels on training examples during training with label corruption.
rows.measure: Effective rank and test accuracy over training; authors report effective rank drops to less than 10% of its initial value and, under high label noise, rises again when test accuracy decreases.
rows.value: figure only for trajectory; stated drop to less than 10% of its initial value in experiments with no random labels
rows.note: The stated effective-rank result is an early-training change; the figure plots its trajectory. It does not directly establish that this property tracks the train-test gap.
rows.check: Effective rank is not magnitude-aware sharpness. The high-noise rebound described in the measure belongs to a different condition.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Measured effective rank of tangent kernels on training examples during training with label corruption.
rows.measure: Effective rank and test accuracy over training; authors state effective rank anti-correlates with test accuracy under high label noise and rises when overfitting starts.
rows.note: The text states the direction of the association but gives no numerical values for this condition.
rows.check: Effective rank does not measure any listed version. The text also supplies an omitted quantitative result: early rank falls below 20% of its initial value with half the labels randomized.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Measured centered kernel alignment between tangent kernels and class-label kernels during training.
rows.measure: Centered kernel alignment with class labels over training; authors report increasing alignment as training progresses.
rows.note: The paper describes increasing alignment but does not report numeric values in the text.
rows.check: Kernel-label alignment does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Measured centered kernel alignment between tangent kernels and class-label kernels during training.
rows.measure: Alignment with clean test labels reaches a higher value during the learning phase than alignment evaluated on training examples with randomized labels.

rows.note: The text explicitly states this comparison and its direction; exact values are not given.
rows.check: The stated alignment comparison is observed, but cannot establish any listed version; its state should not imply observation of a version's effect.
